items.abstract:
<jats:p><p>For more than a century, some corporate founders have wanted to maintain control of their corporations, even after the corporation enters the public market. Many have consolidated around one idea: providing a separate class of common stock with multiple votes per share to the insiders who want to maintain control. These supervoting shares allow insiders to maintain control at a lower cost than acquiring a majority of the outstanding common stock. The control supervoting shares provide to insiders allows them to follow their idiosyncratic vision, even where that delays the corporation’s profitability. It also allows passive investors who do not care about control to invest solely in the corporation’s revenue.</p>
<p>These benefits come at a cost, though. Supervoting shares effectively eliminate shareholder democracy, including the ability of shareholders to police management and hold it responsible. The benefits flow primarily to the insiders who hold supervoting shares, while the costs are spread broadly, not only on shareholders but, sometimes, on society at large. As a result, insiders have an incentive to overuse supervoting shares.</p>
<p>This overuse has become significantly more salient since Google went public in 2004. Today, a significant portion of technology companies include a class of supervoting common shares in their public offerings.</p>
<p>In this Article, I propose that the federal income tax treat classes of supervoting shares as quasi-pass-through interests. That is, rather than wait until a corporation distributes dividends, holders of supervoting shares should include their pro rata share of net corporate income in their gross income in the year the corporation earns that income, irrespective of whether it distributes that income or not. By requiring shareholders of supervoting shares to include their pro rata share of corporate income in their gross income every year, the tax law would increase the net present cost of owning such shares and force would-be supervoting shareholders to evaluate whether having an outsized voting interest in the corporation is worth the cost. I also look at whether this pass-through treatment meets the possibly constitutional realization requirement and determine that, under recent Supreme Court precedent, it does.</p></jats:p>
title: Shareholder Democracy, Dual-Class Equity Structures, and Pass-Through Taxation

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper investigates the pass-through of an excise tax imposed on a monopoly firm with constant marginal cost. The optimal price increases as tax increases for any demand function. Tax pass-through is globally under or in excess of 100% according as the direct demand function is log-concave or log-convex. The analysis relies on supermodular optimization and delivers conclusions based on minimal sufficient assumptions in a simple, broadly accessible and self-contained framework. Further results allow for mixed conditions that provide precise and local determination of pass-through. Several illustrative examples are given. Policy conclusions relating to the relative wisdom of taxing high versus low cost monopoly firms are drawn from the results.</jats:p>
title: On Taxation Pass-Through for a Monopoly Firm

items.abstract: This paper examines the economic effects of the 2012 Kansas tax reform, which sharply reduced individual income tax rates and fully exempted pass-through business income from state taxation. Using a panel of U.S.\states from 2000 to 2017 and the Synthetic Control Method, I construct a counterfactual Kansas to estimate the reform’s causal impact. The reform generated a large and persistent fiscal shock, with state income tax revenue declining sharply relative to the synthetic control. In contrast, there is no evidence of corresponding improvements in real economic performance. Real gross state product, personal income, and wage and salary employment show no meaningful gains, and sectoral outcomes exhibit no sustained expansion. Measures of pass-through activity, particularly proprietor income, increase relative to the synthetic control, though not statistically distinguishable from placebo variation. Overall, the results are inconsistent with a broad supply-side expansion and instead point to an income reclassification mechanism, whereby income shifts into tax-favored categories without corresponding increases in output, employment, or aggregate income.
title: Pass-Through Taxation and Economic Outcomes: Evidence from the Kansas Tax Experiment

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper examines the interaction between output taxation, productivity-enhancing investment, and tax pass-through under Cournot competition. A two-stage n-firm model is developed in which firms first choose cost-reducing investment and subsequently compete in quantities under a specific output tax. Investment reduces marginal production costs and involves a convex investment cost, while firms take the strategic effects of investment on subsequent market competition into account. The model derives the symmetric subgame-perfect equilibrium and characterizes the effects of taxation, investment productivity, and market structure on investment, output, effective marginal cost, and equilibrium prices. The results show that an increase in the output tax reduces both equilibrium output and productivity-enhancing investment. The investment response arises indirectly because taxation reduces the equilibrium production scale and therefore lowers the private return to cost reduction. Lower investment subsequently increases firms' effective marginal production costs. The analysis further shows that greater investment productivity increases both investment and output, while greater competition reduces investment per firm but can increase aggregate industry investment under the maintained parameter conditions. Finally, endogenous investment can amplify tax pass-through and generate tax over-shifting when investment productivity is sufficiently high relative to its cost. These results highlight an investment-mediated channel through which output taxation affects productive efficiency and tax incidence under imperfect competition.</jats:p>
title: Output Taxation, Productive Investment, and Cost Pass-Through under Cournot Competition

<jats:p>Изучено и проанализировано значение малого и среднего предпринимательств в масштабах государства. Был осуществлен анализ, нацеленный на динамику малого бизнеса за предыдущие годы, а также анализ текущей налоговой политики относительно предприятий малого бизнеса. Делается акцент на необходимость реформации системы, так как малый бизнес  основа развития экономики в целом. Статья более всего рассчитана на аудиторию молодых предпринимателей, занимающихся или планирующих заниматься малым бизнесом в какой-либо сфере. Целью перед собой автор ставит ознакомление читателя с некоторыми тонкостями и преградами, с которыми могу с большой долей вероятности столкнутся молодые предприниматели на первых шагах своей деятельности. Рассмотрены не только потенциальные преграды, но и некоторые преимущества и возможности.</jats:p>
                                                                                                            <jats:p>The role of small and medium-sized businesses on a government scale was studied and analyzed. The analysis of the dynamics of small business in the previous years, as well as the analysis of the existing tax policy in relation to small business enterprises. Emphasis is placed on the need to reform the system, since small business is the basis of economic prosperity.</jats:p>
title: Налогообложение малого бизнеса- развитие или барьер?

items.abstract: <jats:p>Development of small business in the USA can be connected with a number of the reasons among which it is possible to call as the features of historical character connected with emergence and development of the United States and the reasons of tax character. So, in each state privileges on taxes which allow to organize in the best way by use of tax planning business can be established. It is represented that the institutionalism is indissoluble with the taxation as in the taxation there are institutes, customs, for example, regarding check of conscientiousness of the taxpayer, use of the special tax treatments and the habits, so at many businessmen and the companies became a habit earlier to pay taxes, to form an overpayment on taxes for the purpose of decrease in risks of additional accrual of penalties, others opposite, created a habit of a conclusion of the capitals abroad to low-tax territories for the purpose of decrease in the tax load. The purpose of formation of institutes is decrease in negative tendencies in the taxation, institutes are capable to improve process of the taxation, including taxation of small business. Improvement of tax administration in the sphere of small business assumes development and realization of actions which, on the one hand, allow to simplify system of tax administration, to reduce a number of hours, spent by taxpayers for stay in taxing authority. At the same time tax administration allows to apply the special modes to small business and to lower administrative load of small business. In various countries various mechanisms of simplification of tax administration for micro and small enterprises are used, a number of mechanisms can be effectively used in the Russian Federation.</jats:p>
title: FEATURES OF THE TAXATION OF SMALL BUSINESS IN THE USA

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study adopts a new approach in assessing the impact of taxes on small business growth and suggests the need to consider new incentives that would be more effective in encouraging small business growth and would also improve the neutrality of the existing tax system.</jats:p>

<jats:p>This paper examines the Small Business Entities (SBE) income tax accounting concessions (for prepaid expenses;  depreciating assets and trading stock ) that replaced the former Simplified Tax System (STS) concessions on 1 July 2007. 

Given that the former STS concessions have been subject to much criticism by commentators, professional and government bodies  this paper firstly tracks the origins of the STS concessions in the 1999 Review of Business Taxation’s (herein after called the ‘Review’) report  and the subsequent legislative fixes up to 30 June 2007.  The paper then examines the SBE income tax accounting concessions and finds that the new SBE framework retains many of the features of the former STS and thus is open to the same criticisms.  The SBE regime though provides a more flexible framework for small business and it is somewhat better integrated with other small business taxation concessions.</jats:p>
title: The Small Business Entities Income Tax Accounting Concessions: Taxation Deja Vous

items.abstract: <jats:p>Among the many contributions that Judith Freedman has made to tax law and policy in the United Kingdom and around the world, one of the most sustained and significant involves the regulation and taxation of small business. This article reviews Professor Freedman’s contributions to tax law and policy regarding small business, and evaluates Canadian experience with the taxation of private companies and their shareholders in light of Professor Freedman’s work. Part II summarizes Professor Freedman’s main conclusions regarding the taxation of small business, addressing both the taxation of similar economic activities conducted through different legal forms and the rationale and effectiveness of special tax preferences for small business. Part III examines Canadian experience with the taxation of private companies and their shareholders, illustrating the ways in which Professor Freedman’s concerns about structural tax differentials and tax preferences for small business have played out in the Canadian context. Part IV concludes with a few observations about how best to promote simplicity, neutrality and coherence in the taxation of small business.</jats:p>
title: Income Taxation of Small Business: Toward Simplicity, Neutrality and Coherence
